<algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <utility>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Abort with a message on any CUDA runtime error\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                          \\\n    do {                                                                          \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s (%s)\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_), #call);                             \\\n            exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                   \\\n        }                                                                         \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Thread block shape: x is the fastest-varying (contiguous) dimension\nconstexpr unsigned int BLOCK_X = 32;\nconstexpr unsigned int BLOCK_Y = 4;\nconstexpr unsigned int BLOCK_Z = 2;\n\n// 3D index calculation\n__host__ __device__ inline size_t idx3(const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z, const size_t nx, const size_t ny) {\n    return z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n}\n\n// Laplacian with clamped boundary conditions\n__device__ __forceinline__ double computeLaplacian(const double* __restrict__ c, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz,\n                                                   const double dx, const double dy, const double dz,\n                                                   const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z) {\n    const size_t xp = (x < nx - 1) ? x + 1 : x;\n    const size_t yp = (y < ny - 1) ? y + 1 : y;\n    const size_t zp = (z < nz - 1) ? z + 1 : z;\n    const size_t xn = (x > 0) ? x - 1 : 0;\n    const size_t yn = (y > 0) ? y - 1 : 0;\n    const size_t zn = (z > 0) ? z - 1 : 0;\n\n    const double center = c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)];\n    const double cxx = (c[idx3(xp, y, z, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(xn, y, z, nx, ny)] - 2.0 * center) / (dx * dx);\n    const double cyy = (c[idx3(x, yp, z, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(x, yn, z, nx, ny)] - 2.0 * center) / (dy * dy);\n    const double czz = (c[idx3(x, y, zp, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(x, y, zn, nx, ny)] - 2.0 * center) / (dz * dz);\n\n    return cxx + cyy + czz;\n}\n\n// Initialize concentration field (one thread per cell)\n__global__ void initConcentrationKernel(double* __restrict__ c, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz) {\n    const size_t vol = nx * ny * nz;\n    const size_t x = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (x >= nx) return;\n\n    for (size_t z = blockIdx.z * blockDim.z + threadIdx.z; z < nz; z += static_cast<size_t>(blockDim.z) * gridDim.z) {\n        for (size_t y = blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y; y < ny; y += static_cast<size_t>(blockDim.y) * gridDim.y) {\n            const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n            // Generate pseudo-random value in [-1, 1]\n            const size_t linear_id = idx;\n            const double pseudo = ((((linear_id + 1) * 1299709) % vol) / static_cast<double>(vol));\n            c[idx] = -1.0 + 2.0 * pseudo;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Compute chemical potential (one thread per cell)\n__global__ void chemicalPotentialKernel(const double* __restrict__ c, double* __restrict__ mu,\n                                        const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz,\n                                        const double dx, const double dy, const double dz,\n                                        const double gamma, const double e_AA, const double e_BB, const double e_AB) {\n    const size_t x = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (x >= nx) return;\n\n    for (size_t z = blockIdx.z * blockDim.z + threadIdx.z; z < nz; z += static_cast<size_t>(blockDim.z) * gridDim.z) {\n        for (size_t y = blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y; y < ny; y += static_cast<size_t>(blockDim.y) * gridDim.y) {\n            const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n            const double cv = c[idx];\n\n            mu[idx] = 4.5 * ((cv + 1.0) * e_AA + (cv - 1.0) * e_BB - 2.0 * cv * e_AB)\n                     + 3.0 * cv + cv * cv * cv\n                     - gamma * computeLaplacian(c, nx, ny, nz, dx, dy, dz, x, y, z);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Cahn-Hilliard update step (one thread per cell)\n__global__ void cahnHilliardUpdateKernel(double* __restrict__ cnew, const double* __restrict__ cold,\n                                         const double* __restrict__ mu,\n                                         const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz,\n                                         const double D, const double dt, const double dx, const double dy, const double dz) {\n    const size_t x = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (x >= nx) return;\n\n    for (size_t z = blockIdx.z * blockDim.z + threadIdx.z; z < nz; z += static_cast<size_t>(blockDim.z) * gridDim.z) {\n        for (size_t y = blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y; y < ny; y += static_cast<size_t>(blockDim.y) * gridDim.y) {\n            const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n            cnew[idx] = cold[idx] + dt * D * computeLaplacian(mu, nx, ny, nz, dx, dy, dz, x, y, z);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Launch configuration covering an nx * ny * nz grid. The y/z grid dimensions\n// are capped at the CUDA limit; the kernels grid-stride over the remainder.\nstatic dim3 makeGrid(const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz) {\n    const size_t gx = (nx + BLOCK_X - 1) / BLOCK_X;\n    const size_t gy = std::min<size_t>((ny + BLOCK_Y - 1) / BLOCK_Y, 65535);\n    const size_t gz = std::min<size_t>((nz + BLOCK_Z - 1) / BLOCK_Z, 65535);\n    return dim3(static_cast<unsigned int>(gx), static_cast<unsigned int>(gy), static_cast<unsigned int>(gz));\n}\n\nstatic dim3 makeBlock() {\n    return dim3(BLOCK_X, BLOCK_Y, BLOCK_Z);\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<double>& c, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t nx, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t ny, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t nz) {\n    // Check for NaN or Inf\n    for (const auto& val : c) {\n        if (std::isnan(val) || std::isinf(val)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: found NaN or Inf value\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Check if values are in reasonable range for concentration field\n    // After Cahn-Hilliard evolution, values should typically remain bounded\n    double minVal = c[0];\n    double maxVal = c[0];\n    for (const auto& val : c) {\n        minVal = std::min(minVal, val);\n        maxVal = std::max(maxVal, val);\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Concentration range: [%.6f, %.6f]\\n\", minVal, maxVal);\n\n    // Values should generally stay within reasonable bounds\n    if (maxVal > 10.0 || minVal < -10.0) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: values out of expected range\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -x <num>     Grid size in X dimension (default: 64)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -y <num>     Grid size in Y dimension (default: same as X)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -z <num>     Grid size in Z dimension (default: same as X)\\n\");\n = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-x\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nx = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-y\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            ny = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-z\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nz = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n  return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (ny == 0) ny = nx;\n    if (nz == 0) nz = nx;\n\n    printf(\"Cahn-Hilliard Phase Separation Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Grid size: %zu x %zu x %zu\\n\", nx, ny, nz);\n    printf(\"Time steps: %d\\n\", iterations);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n\n    // Physical parameters\n    const double dx = 1.0;\n    const double dy = 1.0;\n    const double dz = 1.0;\n    const double dt = 0.01;\n    const double e_AA = -(2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double e_BB = -(2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double e_AB = (2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double gamma = 0.5;\n    const double D = 1.0;\n\n    const size_t gridSize = nx * ny * nz;\n    const size_t bytes = gridSize * sizeof(double);\n\n    // Select device and allocate device-resident fields (outside the timed region)\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(0));\n    double* d_cold = nullptr;\n    double* d_cnew = nullptr;\n    double* d_mu = nullptr;\n    if (gridSize > 0) {\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_cold, bytes));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_cnew, bytes));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_mu, bytes));\n    }\n\n    // Initialize concentration field\n    printf(\"Initializing concentration field...\\n\");\n {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1792983613487,"sessionID":"ses_e89dcb272ffeEjDiOEODba8f8c","part":{"id":"prt_176269f26001Rsq9eZ4MPKcGoF","messageID":"msg_1762697c3001pksS47P0c5kbu3","sessionID":"ses_e89dcb272ffeEjDiOEODba8f8c","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm wondering if we can push the speedup further, since the 3090 run is likely memory-bandwidth bound. Estimating the bytes moved per cell per step for the stencil reads and writes, I work out roughly 40 bytes/cell/step, which across 134M cells and 20 steps lands around 107GB of total memory traffic.\n\nAt 936 GB/s bandwidth that should take about 115ms, but we're measuring 904ms — roughly 8x off the theoretical bound, so there's real headroom. I suspect the culprits are the 64-bit index arithmetic, the clamp-based boundary selects, and the current block shape with grid-stride loops; switching to 32-bit indexing could help since realistic grid sizes never approach the memory needed to exceed 32-bit bounds, though it would require some safeguards or a templated index type. Fusing the kernels to cut global memory round-trips is another option, though a bigger undertaking, and I'm also considering whether a different block/tile shape could improve memory coalescing.\n\nRather than guessing, I want to quickly test a handful of block shape variants — things like 32x4x2, 32x8x1, 64x2x2, 32x2x4, 128x1x1, and 16x8x1 — by copying the source into a temp directory alongside the common headers so I don't touch the repo, then compiling each variant to see which configuration actually performs best.\n\n","time":{"start":1792983605031,"end":1792983613386},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1792983783417,"sessionID":"ses_e89dcb272ffeEjDiOEODba8f8c","part":{"id":"prt_17629301e0014TDye0ywxODxy7","messageID":"msg_176292a46001Ym4lm4oU3z40oV","sessionID":"ses_e89dcb272ffeEjDiOEODba8f8c","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm comparing measured kernel times against bandwidth-bound estimates at 512^3: the update step is running about 5.5x slower than its theoretical 3.4ms, and I'm now working out the same ideal estimate for the chemistry kernel, which should be around 2.3ms.\n\nActually, the real culprit is likely FP64 throughput — the RTX 3090 only runs double-precision at 1/64 the FP32 rate, so with roughly 40 flops per cell across 134M cells, we'd expect ~10ms just from compute, and the divisions by dx*dx in the Laplacian (three per cell, done in double precision) are especially expensive since FP64 division is slow and can't be safely replaced by multiplying by a precomputed reciprocal without changing the result bits for a runtime dx value. That points to the consumer GPU's crippled FP64 rate as the real bottleneck rather than memory bandwidth.\n\nOne exact optimization occurs to me though: when dx*dx equals exactly 1.0, dividing by it is bit-identical to leaving the value unchanged, since IEEE division by 1 is exact. So I could add a runtime check for unit spacing and skip those divisions entirely in that common case without breaking bit-exactness, using a uniform branch that's cheap across a warp.\n\nThis would help both the chem kernel's Laplacian terms and the mu-Laplacian in the update kernel, which also has divisions and sits around 19ms. I'll implement this as a template parameter on the kernels that's dispatched from the host depending on whether the spacing is unit, keeping the non-unit path as a fallback.\n\n","time":{"start":1792983773214,"end":1792983783384},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1792983783745,"sessionID":"ses_e89dcb272ffeEjDiOEODba8f8c","part":{"id":"prt_1762957e2001iSNOSLU1YlncW6","messageID":"msg_176292a46001Ym4lm4oU3z40oV","sessionID":"ses_e89dcb272ffeEjDiOEODba8f8c","type":"text","text":"The profile shows the chemical-potential kernel dominates (26-45 ms per step vs 19 ms for the update), which points to FP64 arithmetic. The RTX 3090 has very low FP64 throughput, and each Laplacian contains three double-precision divisions by `dx*dx`.\n\nWhen the spacing is unit (`dx*dx == dy*dy == dz*dz == 1.0`, the default), dividing by 1.0 is an exact identity in IEEE arithmetic, including for NaN and Inf. So I can add a compile-time specialization that skips the divisions with bit-identical results. I'll implement that now.","time":{"start":1792983783394,"end":1792983783739}}}

Fusing chem into update wouldn't help since it doesn't cut FP64 work, so I think we're near the hardware ceiling for bit-exact FP64 on this card and it's reasonable to stop optimizing here, noting the consumer GPU's FP64 limitation as the bottleneck. I should also double check the CMake build from a fresh directory and verify the nvcc compiler flag quoting produces clean compiles with no warnings under -Wall -Wextra.\n\nThe CMake version fallback architecture list looks fine, and the executable doesn't need special handling for missing GPUs since CUDA is required unconditionally.                                                \\\n18:         if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n19:             fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s (%s)\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__, \\\n20:                     cudaGetErrorString(err_), #call);                             \\\n21:             exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                   \\\n22:         }                                                                         \\\n23:     } while (0)\n24: \n25: // Thread block shape: x is the fastest-varying (contiguous) dimension\n26: constexpr unsigned int BLOCK_X = 32;\n27: constexpr unsigned int BLOCK_Y = 4;\n28: constexpr unsigned int BLOCK_Z = 2;\n29: \n30: // 3D index calculation\n31: __host__ __device__ inline size_t idx3(const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z, const size_t nx, const size_t ny) {\n32:     return z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n33: }\n34: \n35: // Laplacian with clamped boundary conditions.\n36: // UnitSpacing is set when dx*dx, dy*dy and dz*dz all equal 1.0;
